125:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Malt beverage means any alcoholic beverage obtained by the fermentation of any infusion or decoction of barley, malt, hops, or any other similar product, or any combination of such products in water, containing not more than 14 percent alcohol by volume and including ale, porter, brown, stout, lager beer, small beer, and strong beer. The term "malt beverage" does not include sake, known as Japanese rice wine.
Minor means any person less than 19 years of age; provided, however, any person who is 18 years of age or older and who is a member of the regular armed forces of the United States and has a valid active duty military identification card is excepted from this definition.
Person means any individual, firm, partnership, cooperative, nonprofit membership corporation, joint venture, association, company, corporation, agency, syndicate, estate, trust, business trust, receiver, fiduciary, or other group or combination acting as a unit, body politic, or political subdivision, whether public, private, or quasi-public.
Premises means the space or area owned, leased, or controlled by the licensee and used by the licensee for the purpose of operating under the license, the building in which this space or area is located, and the lot on which this building is located.
Retailer or retail dealer means, except as to distilled spirits, any person who sells alcoholic beverages, either in unbroken packages or for consumption on the premises, at retail only to consumers and not for resale.
Wholesaler or wholesale dealer means any person who sells alcoholic beverages to other wholesale dealers, to retail dealers, or to retail consumption dealers.
Wine means any alcoholic beverage containing not more than 24 percent alcohol by volume made from fruits, berries, or grapes either by natural fermentation or by natural fermentation with brandy added. The term "wine" includes, but is not limited to, all sparkling wines, champagnes, combinations of such beverages, vermouths, special natural wines, rectified wines, and like products. The term "wine" does not include cooking wine mixed with salt or other ingredients so as to render it unfit for human consumption as a beverage. A liquid shall first be deemed to be a wine at that point in the manufacturing process when it conforms to this definition.
(Ord. No. 14, § II, 5-11-1982)
129:
The electors of the town, in a June 9, 2020, referendum, by a majority of the electors participating in said referendum, approved the Sunday sale of malt beverages, beer and wine by the package on Sundays, and based upon this authorizing referendum, the town council does hereby readopt and reaffirm the town's malt beverages, beer and wine by this article except as amended herein.
(Ord. No. 14, § IX, 5-11-1982; Ord. No. 20-714, § 4(a)(3), 7-14-2020)
130:
(a) Each applicant for a retail license shall:
(1) Be a person at least 21 years of age.
(2) Be the owner or an employee of a business that has sold merchandise other than malt beverages and wine at retail for at least six months prior to the filing of the application.
(3) State the name of the business of which he/it is an owner or an employee and describe the premises where the products will be sold at retail.
(4) Show by his own affidavit and by filing with the clerk, a copy of his state sales tax records that the business has had minimum gross sales of merchandise other than malt beverages and wine of at least $1,500.00 per month, for the six successive calendar months preceding the filing of his application.
(5) Not have been found guilty of any violation of any law relating to the sale of alcoholic beverages for a period of five years preceding the filing of his application.
(6) Not have had a license issued to him to sell alcoholic beverages revoked by any licensing party for violation of law or its rules within a period of five years immediately preceding the filing of his application.
(7) Not have been convicted of a felony or any crime involving moral turpitude.
(b) Upon approval of the application, the applicant must place an advertisement in a local newspaper of general circulation four times stating the name and address of the applicant, purpose of the application, the location of the business, and must supply an affidavit to the clerk, together with a copy of the advertisement to the effect that such has appeared four times in the local newspaper, and then the license will be issued.
(c) No license to sell malt beverages or wines shall be issued by the city council to or for:
(1) A location within 100 yards of any school, playground for children, any church or funeral chapel, provided such distances shall be measured from the property line of the business premises to the property line of said school, playground, church, or funeral chapel, at the point where the property lines are nearest each other.
(2) A location where the granting of a license would constitute a violation of applicable local, state, or federal laws or regulations.
(Ord. No. 14, § III, 5-11-1982)
131:
(a) Each applicant for a retail or wholesale license for the sale of malt beverages or wine shall make a written application to the city council for the privilege of carrying on the sale of malt beverages or wine at wholesale or retail upon forms furnished and approved by the city clerk. Such application shall be made under oath and filed with the city clerk and shall contain the following information:
(1) The name, age, address and length of residency of the applicant; if the applicant is a corporation, the names of its officers, directors, stockholders and their home addresses.
(2) The trade name, address and description of the premises or place of business which is to be operated under the license.
(3) A complete record of all arrests and convictions against the applicant and every partner, officer, director or stockholder of the applicant of any and all laws and ordinances, city, state or federal.
(4) A statement of whether the applicant, or any person with an interest in the application, has made application at any previous time for any alcoholic beverage license and the disposition of such application.
(5) Whether a previous license issued to the applicant or any person with an interest in the application has been revoked by any state or subdivision thereof or by the federal government and the reason therefor.
(6) Whether any person other than the applicant is to be interested directly or indirectly in the profits or losses or both of the proposed business.
(7) The name of the owner, landlord, or lessor of the proposed location and whether the rent for the premises is to be paid to the landlord or lessor on a percentage of the receipts of the business or contingent upon the amount of business done.
(b) The following documents shall be attached to each application:
(1) Evidence of ownership of the premises where the proposed business is to be located or a copy of the lease if the applicant is leasing the building or premises.
(2) A certified or cashier's check payable to the city for the proper amount of the license fee.
(3) A drawing to scale, showing the nearest school, college, playground, church, or funeral chapel, or an affidavit of a registered surveyor that the proposed location of the business premises complies with section 4-22(c).
(c) Upon completion of the application and the printing of the notice in the newspaper, the city clerk shall submit the application to the city council at its next regularly scheduled meeting and shall notify the applicant of the date, time and place of the meeting. Before the city council shall deny any application or reapplication for a license, or shall revoke any existing license, the applicant or licensee, as the case may be, shall be given notice in writing by the Mayor or the city clerk to show cause before the city council at a time and place specified and being not less than three days nor more than ten days from the date of service of the notice, why the application or reapplication for license should not be denied, or why the license should not be revoked, as the case may be. This notice shall set forth any objections to the application, or reapplication, and any possible grounds on which a denial of the application, or reapplication, or a revocation of the license, may be based as well as the names of any witnesses to be called in support of the denial or revocation. At the appointed time and place, the applicant or licensee shall have an opportunity to present evidence, call witnesses, cross examine witnesses, make statements and otherwise show cause, if any exists, why the application or reapplication should not be denied or why the license should not be revoked. After this hearing and based upon the evidence presented at this hearing, the city council shall take such action as it, in its judgment, shall deem warranted under the facts. The hearing herein provided for need not be at a regular meeting of the city council but may be at such time and place as shall be fixed in the above-described notice.
(d) All malt beverages or wine licenses shall expire at 12:00 midnight on December 31 of the year in which issued.
(e) All applications for renewal of malt beverage or wine licenses shall be filed with the city clerk prior to November 15. All applications for renewal of licenses for the ensuing year shall be treated as applications for new licenses, except that they need not be advertised nor, except to the extent of any change in ownership or interested parties, investigated by the city. All such reapplications shall be acted on by the city council at the December meeting of the city council unless notice is given to any applicant pursuant to subsection (c) of this section.
(Ord. No. 14, § IV, 5-11-1982)

(Ord. No. 14, § VIII(B), 5-11-1982)
133:
(a) The Mayor or the city council shall have the right to suspend any malt beverage or wine license pending the hearing provided for in section 4-23(c), where in the judgment of the Mayor or the city council, such action is necessary to protect the public health, safety, welfare or morals of the community. 134:
(a) The holder of every malt beverage or wine license under this article shall have available in his place of business at all times the current copy of this article and shall be responsible for compliance with this article by all persons on the premises.
(b) Licensed premises operated under this article shall be open to inspection by authorized personnel of the city, at any and all times.

137:
The applicant for a retail license for the sale of malt beverages or wine shall pay to the city clerk, at the time his application is submitted, the sum as indicated on the town's fee schedule, as an annual license fee for the operation for one year at one location or business where the products will be sold.
(Ord. No. 14, § V(A), 5-11-1982)
138:
(a) There is hereby levied and imposed upon each licensee selling malt beverages within the city, an excise tax in the following amounts:
(1) $0.05 per 12-ounce container of malt beverage or portion thereof.
(2) $0.06 per 16-ounce container.
(3) $0.07 for each container in excess of 16 ounces, but less than 32 ounces.
(4) $0.13 per 32-ounce container.
(5) $6.00 per 15½-gallon keg.
(b) There is hereby levied and imposed upon each licensee selling wine within the city, an excise tax in the following amounts:
(1) $0.05 per one-half pint container or less.
(2) $0.10 per pint container.
(3) $0.16 per four-fifths of a quart container.
(4) $0.20 per quart container.
(5) $0.40 per one-half-gallon container.
(6) $0.80 per gallon container.
(c) There shall be levied and imposed on all wine sold within the city, according to the metric system of measure, an excise tax of $0.22 per liter and a proportionate tax at like rates on all fractional parts of a liter.
(d) The taxes described in subsections (a) through (c) of this section shall be collected as provided by the laws of the state.
(e) There is hereby levied and imposed upon each wholesale dealer selling wine within the city, an excise tax of $0.80 per wine gallon. This is based on $0.00625 per ounce at 128 ounces per gallon.
(f) Each licensed wholesale dealer shall include on that report required by state law the name of the retail dealer to whom sales were made for the preceding calendar month and the exact quantity sold to said retailer.
(Ord. No. 14, § V(B)—(G), 5-11-1982)
139:
Any wholesale dealer in malt beverages or wines licensed by the state or the agent of such wholesale dealer shall be granted a permit upon payment, as indicated on the town's fee schedule, annually for malt beverages and annually for wine to distribute such beverages in the city, upon application for such permit to the city clerk, and the presentation of evidence that he understands this article and the conditions under which retail licenses are issued.
(Ord. No. 14, § VI, 5-11-1982)
140:
No license or permit issued under this article shall be transferable. The city council, reserves the right to revoke for cause any license permit issued hereunder without refund of any amount paid therefor.
(Ord. No. 14, § VII, 5-11-1982)
143:
No holder of a license authorizing the sale of malt beverages or wine in the city, nor any agent or employee of the licensee shall do any of the following upon the licensed premises:
(1) Knowingly furnish or cause to be furnished or permit any other person in his employ to serve or furnish malt beverages or wine to a minor as defined in this article.
(2) Employ in any capacity whatsoever as an employee of the licensed premises any person under 18 years of age.
(3) Knowingly sell malt beverages or wine to any person while such person is in an intoxicated condition.
(4) Allow any person under 21 years of age to be in, frequent, or loiter on or within the licensed premises unless such minor is accompanied by a parent or legal guardian.
(5) Permit any disturbance of the peace or obscenity or any lewd, immoral or improper entertainment, conduct or practice on the licensed premises.
(6) Sell or offer for sale malt beverages or wine by use of vending machines.
(7) Sell, offer for sale, possess, or permit the consumption on the licensed premises of any kind of alcoholic beverages, the sale, possession or consumption of which is not authorized under the license.
(8) Add to the contents of a bottle or refill empty bottles or in any other manner misrepresent the quantity, quality, or brand name of any malt beverage or wine.
(9) Receive or cause to be delivered at the licensed premises any alcoholic beverages by any means other than by a conveyance owned and operated by a wholesale dealer with a permit and license from the city to make such deliveries.
(10) Permit or allow the consumption of malt beverages, wine, or any other alcoholic beverages on the licensed premises.
(11) Make or allow to be made any false statement on any application, reapplication, or other documents required to be furnished by federal, state or local law, regulations or ordinances.
(12) Violate, either personally or through an agent or employee, any federal, state or local law, regulation or ordinance, except traffic violations. The determination of whether any such violation has occurred shall be made by the city council and a formal accusation, indictment, charge or conviction by a governmental agency for such offense shall not be necessary in order to suspend or revoke the license.
(13) Make deliveries of any malt beverage or wine beyond the boundaries of the premises covered by the license.
(14) Store any malt beverages or wine anywhere other than the premises for which the license is issued.
(15) Allow or permit pool, billiards or any game of a similar nature to be played or engaged in on the premises where such business is conducted.
(Ord. No. 14, § VIII(A)(1)—(16), 5-11-1982)
144:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to hold a malt beverage or wine license who also has any direct financial interest in any wholesale malt beverage or wine license.
(b) It shall be unlawful for the holder of any retail license to accept or receive financial aid or assistance from the holder of any manufacturer's or wholesaler's license.
(c) No person shall knowingly and intentionally act as an agent to purchase or acquire any malt beverages or wine for or on behalf of any minor, or otherwise procure for or furnish to a minor any alcoholic beverage, except for medical purposes upon the written prescription of a duly licensed physician under the laws of the state.
(d) It shall be unlawful for any minor to falsely represent his or her age in any manner whatsoever in violation of this article or other applicable laws.
(e) It shall be unlawful for any minor to purchase, drink or possess any alcoholic beverage in the city.
(Ord. No. 14, § VIII(E)—(H), 5-11-1982)
148:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Alcoholic beverages means malt beverages and wines, as defined herein, and shall include any beverage containing wine.
Amusement center means any business which has a seating capacity of at least 10,000 people or any type of sporting event, including a golf course and drag racing.
Governing authority means the city council.
Hotel means a building or other structure with a restaurant kept, used maintained, advertised and held out to the public to be a place where sleeping accommodations are offered for adequate pay to travelers and guest whether transient, permanent, or residential, in which 100 or more rooms are used for the sleeping accommodations of such guests. Motels meeting the qualifications set out herein for hotels shall be classified in the same category as hotels. Hotels shall have the privilege of granting franchises for the operation of a lounge and restaurant in their premises and the holder of such franchise shall be included in the definition of hotel thereunder.
License means the authorization by the governing authority to engage in the sale for consumption on the premises of malt beverage and wine.
Licensee means any person, firm, corporation, partnership or association duly licensed by the governing authority to sell by the drink and for consumption only on the premises malt beverages and wine.
Lounge means a separate room connected with, a part of and adjacent to a restaurant or located in hotels, as defined herein, with all booths, stools, and tables being unobstructed and open to view. A lounge shall be air conditioned and have a seating capacity of at least 75 persons.
Premises means the space or area owned, leased and/or controlled by the licensee and used for the purposes of operating under the license which shall be a definite closed or partitioned-in locality whether a room, shop, or building, wherein malt beverages and wine shall be sold and consumed therein; except that in the case of hotels and motels, the term "premises" includes only the portion of the property where alcoholic beverages are sold; except, further, that in the case of an amusement center, as defined herein, the term "premises" shall include the geographic grounds of the amusement center, including without limitation, the spectator stands, seating, and playing area of the golf course; and except further that in the case of restaurants, the term "premises" includes a deck or patio that is adjacent to and contiguous with the restaurant. The term "premises" also means one physically identifiable place of business consisting of one room, or two or more contiguous rooms operating under the same name where alcoholic beverages are sold. Any premises which cannot be determined as one identifiable place of business shall require additional licenses regardless of such establishments having the same name, ownership or management. In the case of a licensee where a golf course is located adjacent to and contiguous with a restaurant (club house), the term "premises" shall include the playing area of the golf course.
Residence means the place where one actually lives as distinguished from his domicile or place of temporary sojourn.
Resident means a person whose primary residence is within the territorial limits of the city.
Restaurant means any public place kept, used, maintained, advertised and held out to the public as a place where meals are prepared and served, and where meals are actually and regularly prepared and served, without sleeping accommodations, such place being provided with adequate and sanitary kitchen and dining room equipment and seating capacity of at least 75 people, having employed therein a sufficient number and kind of employees to prepare, cook and serve suitable food for its guests. At least two meals a day shall be served at least six days a week, with the exception of holidays, vacations and periods of redecorating, and the serving of such meals shall be the principal business conducted, with the serving of malt beverages and wines consumed on the premises as only incidental thereto.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 1)
149:
The ordinance from which this article is derived was adopted by the city council on July 14, 2020, and pursuant to a June 9, 2020, referendum held by the town, and in which a majority of the electors voting in said June 9, 2020, referendum approved the sale of distilled spirits by the drink for consumption only on the premises, and approved the Sunday sale of alcoholic beverages.
(Ord. No. 20-714, § 2(a)(4), 7-14-2020)
150:
The electors of the town, in a June 9, 2020, referendum, by a majority of the electors participating in said referendum, approved the sale of distilled spirits by the drink for consumption only on the premises and approved Sunday sales of alcoholic beverages, and based upon this authorizing referendum, the town council does hereby readopt and reaffirm the town's malt beverages, beer and wine by the drink for consumption only on the premises ordinance except as amended herein.
(Ord. No. 20-714, § 2(a)(5), 7-14-2020)
153:
It shall be unlawful for any person to sell or offer to sell any alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises without first complying with the rules and regulations set out in this division.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 2)
154:
No alcoholic beverages shall be sold by the drink for consumption on the premises except under a license granted by the governing authority. Application for a consumption on the premises license shall be made on forms provided by the governing authority as follows:
(1) A consumption on the premises license shall be valid only for the calendar year indicated thereon and no such license may be renewed. A licensee who desires to continue in business during the next subsequent calendar year must make a new application for such year, which need not be advertised.
(2) In addition to the completion and submission of the application form as required by the governing authority, such applicant shall attach thereto a complete application form which with all attachments is required for a state license to sell distilled spirits on the premises.
(3) A notice of each application shall be advertised in the official legal organ paper of the county once a week for two weeks immediately preceding the meeting of the governing authority that the application is to be acted upon.
(4) Any applicant for a consumption on the premises license must show, to the satisfaction of the governing authority, financial responsibility.
(5) Every applicant for a city alcoholic beverage license shall be at least 21 years of age and shall make application on forms furnished by the clerk to the city and in connection therewith shall, under oath, answer all questions, supply all information, and furnish all certificates, affidavits, bonds and other supporting data as required thereby. In all cases where the owner of such business is a resident individual, the application shall be made in his/her name. Where the owner is a firm, corporation, partnership, association, or nonresident, the application shall be made in the name of the resident officer, partner, or associate who owns a substantial interest in the business or in the name of the principal resident managing officer or managing agent and the application shall show that the license is for the use of the owner, and the owner shall be named. The written application for the license shall be a permanent record which the licensee must maintain current as required by this section. Failure to maintain a current license application as required by this section shall be grounds for revocation of the same.
a. No person shall have, own or enjoy any ownership, interest in, share in the profits from, or otherwise participate in the business of any alcoholic beverage licensee in the city unless a full description of such interest shall have been furnished the governing authority at the time such interest arose. It shall be the duty of the licensee to report to the governing authority, within five days any change in any interest in licensee's business, including, but not limited to:
1. Any division of the profits;
2. Any division of net or gross sales for any purposes whatsoever;
3. Any change in the payment of rents or leases;
4. Any change in the ownership of any lease or building or land used in such business; or
5. Any change in the ownership of any corporation, firm, partnership or association that has any interest in such business or the change of management of such corporation, firm, partnership or association.
b. After receipt of such notice, the governing authority shall notify such person within a reasonable time of any objection to the ownership or interest set forth therein, and it shall then be incumbent upon each person to dispose of such interest within 30 days after the mailing of the notice to do so by the governing authority to such person at his address as shown on such notice of interest. In the event such interest is not disposed of within 30 days after the mailing of the notice by the governing authority, or in the event no objections are filed within said 30-day period, or in the event such person fails to notify the governing authority of the transfer of any such interest within 20 days after the acquisition thereof, then the license, as provided for herein, may be revoked by the governing authority until the disposition of the interest has been made or notice given to the governing authority of the transfer.
c. The report required by this section shall be in the form required by the governing authority and shall be an amendment to the licensee's permanent license application on file with the governing authority and as such shall be under oath and verified as otherwise required of license applications.
(6) The city license issued shall be valid only for the calendar year indicated thereon. A licensee that desires to continue in business during the next or subsequent calendar year must make a renewal application for such year on or before November 15 of the preceding year. Payment of the license fee for the renewal of a license shall be made at the time of the application, and upon approval by the governing authority and payment of the fee the renewal license will be issued.
a. No city license may be transferred from one person to another or from one location to another without the permission and approval of the governing authority upon written application made. Approvals as to any change shall be made at the discretion of the governing authority.
b. Each application for transfer of a license shall have attached thereto a completed copy of the notice of change of interest required by the state revenue commissioner. After the receipt of such application, the governing authority shall notify such applicant within 20 days of any objection to the transfer as set forth in the application. Said license shall remain in effect pending approval of the transfer. Upon proper application, the governing authority may permit the license to be transferred upon payment of a transfer fee equal to one-half of the original license fee, provided that the transferee meets all of the qualifications which would have been required had the transferee originally been an applicant for an alcoholic beverage license. Upon the death of any licensee, his personal representative or his heirs may continue to operate under the said license for the balance of the year without the payment of any fee, if otherwise qualified as a licensee, or the license may be transferred to a qualified transferee within 30 days after the condition of the estate of the deceased licensee will permit, upon payment of the above transfer fee.
c. Any licensee desiring to discontinue business at one location and commence business at some other location must make a complete new application for such location.
d. All licenses issued pursuant to this chapter shall be valid only so long as the licensee is actively engaged in such business, with the exception of holidays, vacations, and periods of redecoration, and in the event the licensee shall cease to be actively engaged in such business the licensee shall immediately notify the governing authority and return the license to the governing authority.
(7) The governing authority may, in its discretion, require a personal statement of any employee of any licensee.
(8) When contrary to the public interest and welfare no license to sell alcoholic beverages of any kind shall be issued by the governing authority to or for:
a. Any person as determined by the governing authority by reason of such person's business experience, financial standing, trade association, personal associations, record of arrest, or reputation in any community in which he has resided, who is not likely to maintain the operation for which he is seeking a license in conformity with federal, state, or local laws, rules and regulations.
b. Any person who has been convicted under any federal, state, or local law of any felony involving moral turpitude.
c. Any person who has been convicted under any federal, state, or local law of any felony not involving moral turpitude within ten years immediately preceding the filing of an application for such license.
d. Any person convicted under any federal, state or local law of a misdemeanor, particularly, but not limited to, those involving alcoholic beverages, gambling, or tax law violations, if such conviction tends to indicate that the applicant will not maintain the operation for which he is seeking a license in conformity with federal, state or local laws, rules and regulations.
e. A location not suitable in the judgment and discretion of the governing authority because of traffic congestion, general character of the neighborhood, or by reason of the effect which such an establishment would have on the adjacent and surrounding properties, or in the neighborhood.
f. A location within an area where, in the judgment of the governing authority, the number of alcoholic beverage licenses already granted makes it contrary to the public interest and welfare.
g. A location at which a previous license has been revoked or suspended and where, in the judgment of the governing authority, the problems which have arisen from the operation of the licensee at such location indicate that it is not in the interest of public health, safety, welfare or morals that the sale of alcoholic beverages be permitted at such location.
h. Which the granting of such license would constitute a violation of state law or regulations.
i. The operation of a alcoholic beverage business hereunder by any person, firm, partnership, association or corporation, already holding two such licenses.
j. Any person who is an official of or employee of the city.
k. Any person who is as close kin as brothers or sisters, by blood or marriage, to one already holding an alcoholic beverage license hereunder.
l. Any person to operate a restaurant, hotel, lounge or amusement center except as defined herein. Consumption on the premises sales shall be made in no other place or establishments.
(9) Before the governing authority shall deny any application for a license or for the transfer of any license, or shall revoke any existing license, the applicant or licensee, as the case may be, shall be given notice in writing from the clerk of the governing authority to show cause before the governing authority at a time and place specified therein not less than three days nor more than ten days from the date of service of the notice, why said application for license or for transfer of license should be denied or why said license should not be revoked, as the case may be, stating the grounds therefor, and at the appointed time and place the applicant or licensee shall have the opportunity to show cause, if any exist, why said application should not be denied or said license revoked or suspended, after which the governing authority shall take such action as it, in its judgment and discretion, shall deem warranted under the facts. The hearing herein provided for need not be a regular meeting of the governing authority but may be at such time and place as shall be fixed in said notice. All decisions, denying, approving, suspending or revoking any permit, license, or application shall be in writing, with the reasons therefore stated, and mailed or delivered to the applicant. In addition, at any hearing as provided herein, the party afforded the hearing shall have the opportunity to present evidence and cross examine the opposing witnesses.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 3)
155:
Any applicant for a consumption on the premises license must be of good character and all managers, clerks and other employees who receive, inventory, dispense, serve or are in any way connected with the alcoholic beverages shall be of like character or the application will not be considered. Corporate applicants shall be of good business reputation.
(1) No applicant for a license who has a criminal record (except minor traffic offenses) shall be granted a license.
(2) The governing authority, at their discretion, may consider the extenuating circumstances which may reflect favorably or unfavorably on the applicant, application or proposed location of the business. If, in their judgment, circumstances are such that the granting of the license would not be in the best interest of the general public, such circumstances may be grounds for denying the application.
(3) All applicants, managers, clerks and other employees who receive inventory, dispense, serve or are in any way connected with the alcoholic beverages shall be subject to investigation by the sheriff's department of the county or the town marshal or other police agency designated by the governing authority.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 4)
156:
All applications for licenses to sale alcoholic beverages by the drink for consumption on the premises shall be presented in person by the applicant.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 5)
157:
No consumption on the premises license shall be transferable or assignable to any person or other location, and in the event that a licensed business is sold or closed, it shall be the duty of the licensee to immediately surrender his license to the governing authority.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 6)
158:
No consumption on the premises license shall be granted to any person unless the entire business premises of the proposed location is situated beyond 600 feet from any church building, and beyond 600 feet from any residence, school ground, or college campus, or an alcoholic treatment center. Said distance shall be measured in all directions from the nearest wall enclosing the proposed premises where alcoholic beverages are to be sold to the nearest point of any residence, school, college campus, alcoholic treatment center, or church building. Each application for a consumption on the premises license shall include a scale drawing of the location of the proposed premises showing the distance to the nearest church, school, college campus or residence, or a certificate of a registered surveyor that such location complies with this article with reference to this section.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 7)
159:
A separate consumption on the premises license shall be required for each place of business.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 8)
160:
No consumption on the premises license shall be issued to any person unless the building in which the business will be located is complete, and detailed plans of said building, clearly delineating the area therein where alcoholic beverages shall be sold and consumed, and also the outside of the premises are attached to the application or unless proposed plans and specifications and a building permit of a proposed building to be built are attached to the application. The completed building or the proposed building shall comply with all resolutions of the county or city regulations of the state revenue commissioner, and the laws of the state. The proposed building shall also be subject to final inspection and approval when completed by the governing authority. Each building in which the business will be located shall contain sufficient lighting so that the building itself and the premises on all sides of the building are readily visible at all times from the front of the street on which the building is located as to reveal all of the outside premises of said building. Each applicant for a consumption on the premises license shall attach to his application evidence of ownership of the building or proposed building or a copy of the lease if the applicant is leasing the building. All premises for which a consumption on the premises license shall be issued shall afford therein adequate sanitary toilet facilities and shall be adequately illuminated so that all hallways, passageways and open areas may be clearly seen by customers therein.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 9)
161:
(a) The lot on which the building is located shall have a minimum frontage on a major street or state highway of at least 50 feet and a minimum land area of one acre.
(b) The proposed building shall be set back at least 50 feet from the street or highway right-of-way.
(c) The building must contain a minimum of 2,000 square feet, as measured along the exterior walls; amusement centers are excepted.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 10)
162:
No licensee shall furnish, sell, or offer for sale any alcoholic beverages at any of the following times:
(1) At any time on Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day;
(2) At any time in violation of a local resolution or regulation of a special order of the governing authority; or
(3) During any election day, federal, state or local during the time beginning one hour prior to the opening of the polls and ending one hour after the closing of the polls.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 11; Ord. No. 20-714, § 2(a)(1), 7-14-2020)
163:
No licensee shall give, sell or offer to sell any alcoholic beverages to any person who is under the age of 21 years, or who is noticeably intoxicated, or who is obviously of unsound mind and such fact known to said licensee, or who is a habitual drunkard whose intemperate habits are known to said licensee. At any time, a state driver's license shall be considered the only legal proof of age which would relieve a person making the sale from responsibility thereof.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 12)
164:
No licensee shall keep any alcoholic beverages stored in any bonded or other type warehouse in the city nor shall he enter into any type of an arrangement whereby alcoholic beverages ordered by him are stored by him by any licensed wholesaler. A licensee shall keep no inventory or stock of alcoholic beverages at any place except his licensed place of business and within his licensed place of business his storage place for alcoholic beverages shall be immediately adjacent to the room where he is licensed to do business.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 13)
165:
(a) The annual fee for a consumption on the premises for malt beverages shall be as set forth on the city's fee schedule and shall be paid prior to the issuance of any license; said fee to accompany the application and shall be either in cash or a bank certified check. Any person who is doing business or begins to do business at any time after January 1 and before July 1 shall pay the full licensee fee. Any person who begins to do business on or after July 1 shall pay a prorated annual fee, and in the case of a revocation or surrender of such license, the license holder is not entitled to receive any refund.
(b) The annual fee for consumption on the premises for wines shall be as set forth on the city's fee schedule and shall be paid prior to the issuance of any license; said fee to accompany the application and shall be either in cash or a bank certified check. Any person who is doing business or begins to do business at any time after January 1 and before July 1 shall pay the full licensee fee. Any person who begins to do business on or after July 1 shall pay a prorated annual fee, and in the case of a revocation or surrender of such license, the license holder is not entitled to receive any refund.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 14)
166:
In addition to all other requirements, no license for consumption on the premises shall be issued to any applicant who does not meet the requirements of a restaurant, hotel, lounge, or amusement center, as defined herein.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 24)
167:
The following shall be grounds for the suspension and/or revocation of a license. Whether or not said grounds exist shall be determined by the governing authority in its sole discretion:
(1) The violation by the license holder or his employee of any state or federal law or regulation, except misdemeanors, or any resolution of the county or city, other than traffic violations. The determination of whether such violation has occurred shall be made by the governing authority and an actual conviction in a court for such offense shall not be necessary in order to suspend or revoke the license.
(2) The failure of the license holder or his employee to report promptly to the sheriff's department or town marshal any violation of law or of this resolution, breach of peace, disturbance or altercation resulting in violence, occurring on the premises.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 33)
170:
(a) There is hereby levied and imposed upon each wholesale dealer selling malt beverages within the city an excise tax in the following amounts:
(1) Where malt beverages, commonly known as tap or draft beer, are sold in or from a barrel or bulk container, a tax of $6.00 on each container sold containing not more than 15½ gallons and a proportionate tax at the same rate on all fractional parts of 15½ gallons.
(2) Where malt beverages are sold in bottles, cans, or other containers, except barrel or bulk containers, a tax of $0.05 per 12 ounces and a proportionate tax at the same rate on all fractional parts of 12 ounces.
(b) There is hereby levied and imposed upon each wholesale dealer selling wines within the city an excise tax in the amount of $0.22 per liter and a proportionate tax at like rates on all fractional parts of a liter. Said license fees and excise tax shall be collected and paid as provided by the laws of the state.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 15)
173:
In addition to the requirements of wholesalers as set out in this article, the following shall apply:
(1) All wholesale dealers or distributors shall be licensed by the state department of revenue and shall comply with all laws and regulations of the state revenue department before they sell or deliver alcoholic beverages in the city. Deliveries and sales shall be made only to establishments licensed by the city and all deliveries shall be made in vehicles owned and operated by such wholesale dealer or distributor.
(2) Upon each and every delivery by a licensed wholesaler to a licensed retailer, an invoice in triplicate shall be prepared showing the quantities and brands of alcoholic beverages delivered, together with the price thereof, and the excise tax due and collected thereon, the original of such invoice shall be delivered by the wholesaler to the retailer simultaneously with such delivery. The wholesaler shall retain the second copy of such invoice for a period of 12 months after the date of delivery and during such 12-month period, such invoices shall be made available for inspection by the governing authority or its duly authorized representative. Upon request of the city, a copy of such invoice shall be attached to the reports requested or required by the city.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 16)
174:
Licensees under the provisions of this article shall not buy or accept deliveries of alcoholic beverages from wholesalers, dealers, or distributors, except who are licensed by the state revenue department.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 17)
175:
Licensees under the provisions of this article shall keep and maintain the original invoice of each purchase from a wholesaler of any alcoholic beverages for at least 12 months after the date of such purchase, and shall maintain records to show the sales of alcoholic beverages by the drink and other records as required by the city. The city or its duly authorized representative shall have the right to inspect the records of each licensee and make a complete audit of the records pertaining to alcoholic beverages at any time. Failure of a licensee to properly maintain records showing receipt of alcoholic beverages, payment therefor, and payment of the taxes due thereon, shall be unlawful and a violation of this article.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 18)
176:
All holders of a consumption on the premises license shall keep a copy of this article in his premises and shall instruct any person working there with respect to the terms hereof. The licensee shall be held responsible for any acts of his employees in violation of this article, of the laws of the state, or the rules and regulations of the state, and/or the state revenue commissioner.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 19)
177:
The business premises of the holder of a consumption on the premises license for the sale of alcoholic beverages shall be open to inspection at any and all times by officers or officials authorized to conduct such inspections by the governing authority.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 20)
178:
The making of any false statements on an application for a license to sell alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises shall constitute grounds for revocation of said license.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 21)
179:
There shall be no gambling, betting, games of chance, punchboards, slot machines, lotteries or tickets of chance in any licensee's place of business or in any room adjoining the same, which is owned, leased or controlled by licensee. Any violation of this division shall be cause for suspension or revocation of said license.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 22)
180:
Licenses under this article shall be displayed prominently at all times on the premises for which the same was issued.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 23)
181:
Amusement centers may dispense and sell alcoholic beverages in plastic cups.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 25)
182:
Amusement centers must be well maintained with adequate security, and may sell alcoholic beverages one hour before the event and up until the last event which was scheduled.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 26)
183:

(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 27; Ord. No. 20-714, § 2(a)(2), 7-14-2020)
184:
A licensee shall not display signs advertising directly or indirectly, the sale of alcoholic beverages other than in the principal building for which the license is issued. Any sign placed on the licensed premises, within view of the general public, and with the intent to bring attention to the fact that alcoholic beverages can be bought at that location shall be in violation of this section. Licensees shall be permitted to advertise by means of radio, TV, or newspaper, provided that brand names of alcoholic beverages not be used.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 28)
185:
(a) Restaurants shall maintain at least 50 percent of their business volume from the sale of food. This requirement will also apply to any business with consumption on the premises license, and including amusement centers but excluding farm wineries. Food sales shall include all consumable items sold on the premises except alcoholic beverages. (b) Monthly reports for the preceding month's alcohol and food sales shall be submitted on forms provided by the town on or before the 15th day of the month.

(d) Authorized officials of the town may examine the records of businesses licensed hereunder at any reasonable time to ascertain that the requirements of this and other provisions of this article are met.

186:
Any alleged violation of this division shall be reported by any person to the clerk of the governing authority who shall have the power, in his/her discretion to suspend the license for a period not to exceed ten days pending a hearing before the governing authority on the question of whether or not the license shall be revoked for cause or suspended, pursuant to this division.

188:
All licensees for the sale of alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises shall remove or cause to be removed, from the area of the premises utilized by customer or patrons, all alcoholic beverages within 45 minutes after the closing time for the sale of said alcoholic beverages.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 32)
189:

(b) The sale of alcoholic beverages for consumption by persons in any back room or side room which is not open to general public use is prohibited except that private parties or conventions, which have been scheduled in advance, may be served in public or private dining rooms or meeting rooms and provided, further, that this prohibition shall not apply to the registered guests of any hotel or motel in their designated rooms, or the playing areas of golf courses.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 34)
190:
It shall be unlawful for any person to hold a license who has any direct financial interest in any wholesale alcoholic beverage business. It shall be unlawful for the holder of a license to accept or receive financial aid or assistance from the holder of any alcoholic beverage manufacturer's or wholesale dealer's license.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 35)
191:
No trade name, corporate name or name of a business shall be allowed to use the words "beer," "wine," or "beer and wine" in such name.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 36)
192:
Any person violating the rules and regulations set out in this division shall be subject to revocation and/or suspension of his license and punishment as prescribed by the governing authority. 193:
All malt beverages and wine shall be consumed only on the premises.

194:
No licensee shall sell or offer for sale alcoholic beverages by use of vending machines.

(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 40)
196:
If any clause, sentence, paragraph, section or part of this article shall be adjudged by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, such judgment shall not affect, impair or invalidate the remainder of this article.
(Res. of 10-27-1998(2), § 41)
197:
Notwithstanding anything in this article to the contrary, the sale of alcoholic beverages in the city is a privilege, and not a right and the issuance of a license hereunder shall not create any property rights in the license holder.
